lessons.title: From device to samples
lessons.teaches: How collection turns a device on the network into samples the component owns, and where along the way work can be lost.

steps.title: A component answers on the network
steps.prose: Every monitored device is a component. This one is simulated: a simulator beside the outpost answers on its address, speaking the product's protocols, so collection reads it as real hardware. The hits count each poll that reached it.

steps.title: Each poll becomes a sample
steps.prose: The outpost polls the component on a schedule and turns each answer into samples: a number for a metric, a value for a property. The component owns them. Here are its metrics as they stand now, each with its latest value.

steps.title: Delivery is measured hop by hop
steps.prose: Between the poll and the store, a sample crosses several hops. Each hop counts what came in and what went out, so loss is a ratio you read the same way everywhere: 0% is healthy. Pick a hop to see what it does.

lessons.title: Reach and collection
lessons.teaches: How Omniglass decides a device is reachable, rung by rung, and how to tell a network problem from a device problem.

steps.title: The reach ladder
steps.prose: Reach is judged in rungs, in order: reachable (the address answers), responsive (the protocol speaks back), authenticated (the device accepts our credentials). The first rung that fails is where to look. On the component's page, test an endpoint's poll to run one now and see what it read, or the real cause it was refused.

steps.title: Break the network on purpose
steps.prose: A simulated component can be impaired: unplugged, slowed, or dropping packets. Open its simulation and add loss to watch the reach ladder and the delivery figures notice.

lessons.title: Rules and alarms
lessons.teaches: How an event rule turns samples into an alarm: a threshold, a sustain so one bad sample never pages, and a clear.

steps.title: Write a threshold, preview it
steps.prose: An event rule reads one metric or property and says when it is bad. Pick a metric this component reports, set a threshold, and preview: the rule runs against the last day of real samples and shows what it would have fired, writing nothing.

steps.title: Read a shipped rule
steps.prose: Omniglass ships rules for what every fleet needs. reachability-lost fires when a device stops answering and holds for 15 seconds first, so one missed poll never opens an alarm.

steps.title: Trip it with a simulated fault
steps.prose: Open the simulation, tick Unplugged and save: the simulated component goes dark on every protocol, as if its cable were pulled.

steps.title: Watch the alarm open
steps.prose: The outpost finds the component down on its next poll, the rule waits out its 15 second sustain, and an alarm opens, listed here as it lands. Plug it back in the same way and the rule clears it.

lessons.title: Health and impact
lessons.teaches: How an alarm moves health: the component's, then the system it serves, then the place the system sits.

steps.title: An alarm moves the component
steps.prose: A component's health is the worst of its open alarms, by severity. A severity that takes a component out makes it down; a lesser one degrades it.

steps.title: The component moves its systems
steps.prose: A system is the room's AV built to a standard, with slots its components fill. When a component in a slot is down, the slot is short and the system reads degraded or down. These are the systems this component serves.

lessons.title: Acting on it
lessons.teaches: What to do with an alarm: acknowledge it so the team knows it is owned, snooze it while you work, or send the device a command.

steps.title: Acknowledge or snooze
steps.prose: Acknowledging says someone owns the alarm; it stays open until its rule clears it. Snoozing holds its notifications for a while without hiding it.

steps.title: Issue a command
steps.prose: A command tells the device to do something, through its driver: power it on, switch an input. Each command is tracked until the device confirms it or it times out.

lessons.title: Reading the history
lessons.teaches: How to read what happened afterwards: every event, alarm and command lands on the component's activity, in order.

steps.title: The activity is the story
steps.prose: Every event a rule wrote, every alarm opened and cleared, and every command issued is kept on the component's activity, newest first. Read it bottom up to replay an incident.

steps.title: Health over time
steps.prose: A system's health is recorded each time it changes, so its history shows how long it was degraded and when it recovered.
